title: Adaptive license experiment: usage-tiered fees + staged upgrade cadence for on-prem & VPC
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Validate a hybrid pricing and upgrade model for Private/VPC and on-prem customers that balances predictable license revenue with flexibility for spikes. Hypothesis: Offering a small fixed license fee + a usage tier (vCPU/GPU-hours or inference-units) and three support tiers (Standard, Enterprise, Mission Critical) with a staggered upgrade cadence (Quarterly minor, Semi-annual major) will increase win-rate on enterprise RFQs by >=12% while preserving average ARR per deal. Metrics: win-rate vs baseline, ARR per seat/commit, churn after first 12 months, #of SQ (security questionnaire) blockers, average health score post-deploy. Experiment design: 6-month pilot with three cohorts (A: fixed-heavy pricing, B: hybrid fixed+usage (our target), C: usage-heavy pricing) across 12 sales opportunities matched for size and industry. Rollouts: test in EMEA and NA with one APAC pilot account. Support tiers: Standard (business hours, 24h median response), Enterprise (24/7 escalation, prioritized capacity), Mission Critical (SLA-backed hotfix cadence, on-call rotation, dedicated TAM). Upgrade cadence: built into contract as scheduled upgrade windows with opt-in emergency patches. Security & SQ workstream: create a pre-filled SQ template for tiered entitlements, add KMS/HSM choices, list upgrade maintenance windows, and a compliance appendix for air-gapped installs. Acceptance criteria: clear lift in conversion or reduction of negotiation time; <15% of deals needing bespoke legal addenda; SQ issues reduced by 40% compared to baseline. Deliverables: pricing playbook, sales cheat sheet, legal term templates, SQ runbook, telemetry dashboard queries, pilot contract, engineering feature backlog for entitlement enforcement and upgrade tooling.
